agent_summary:
Tested session management on the OWASP Juice Shop host (juice.lab.test, cleartext HTTP only, no test accounts so read-only/unauthenticated probing plus forged-token tests).

Key findings (recorded as leads):
- CRITICAL token forgery (x65-x69, x116, x118, x119): the backend accepts unsigned JWTs with "alg":"none". A hand-crafted token {data:{id:1}} with empty signature is accepted as the admin session on every express-jwt endpoint — /api/Users, /api/Addresss, /api/Complaints, /rest/basket/1, /rest/wallet/balance, and /rest/user/authentication-details/ (which then dumps password hashes, totpSecret and deluxeToken for all users). Control tests prove it: no token, a garbage token, and a bad-signature HS256 token all return 401. So anyone can impersonate any user without credentials.
- Session cookie weaknesses (x7): the token is reflected into Set-Cookie: token=...; Path=/ with no HttpOnly, Secure or SameSite, over cleartext HTTP — scriptable, cleartext, and auto-sent cross-site.
- CSRF (x16/x17/x53/x78): server-rendered /profile and /dataerasure authenticate from the SameSite-less token cookie and their POST forms have no cookie-independent anti-CSRF token.
- No server-side logout / token revocation (x18); tokens have no enforced expiry on the alg:none path (x65) — a captured/forged token stays valid.

Per-item: schema (1), cookie attributes (2), fixation (3, not applicable - tokens are cryptographically bound, invalid values rejected), exposed variables (4, token in non-HttpOnly cookie; no token in URLs per access log), CSRF (5), logout (6), timeout (7, no exp enforced; legit TTL unmeasurable without accounts), puzzling (8, inconsistent header-vs-cookie token sources confirmed x119/x120), hijacking (9) — all done.

Also broadly mapped the host surface (auth-gated /api and /rest endpoints returning 401 unauthenticated, public catalog/feedback/security-question endpoints, /ftp and /support/logs directory listings with null-byte allowlist bypass and downloadable incident-support.kdbx, open /metrics and /rest/admin/application-configuration, wildcard CORS, allowlist-substring open redirect) — these overlap other lanes and were only noted in passing. The alg:none forgery is the headline session issue and should be validated by a person; it likely also belongs to the authentication/authorization lanes.

leads.title: [agent] CSRF: cookie-authenticated /profile page, SameSite-less token cookie, no anti-CSRF token

detail.text: The server-rendered /profile page authenticates from the token cookie (invalid token cookie triggers a decode failure at build/routes/userProfile.js:69, exchanges x16/x17). The token cookie is issued without a SameSite attribute (x7). The profile page's username-change form (POST /profile) has no cookie-independent anti-CSRF token. An attacker page can therefore auto-submit a cross-origin POST /profile using the victim's ambient token cookie to change their profile/username. Writes are disabled in this lane so the POST was not submitted; this is the design-level CSRF exposure. A person should validate with an authenticated session.

leads.title: [agent] No server-side logout / JWT revocation; tokens valid until expiry

detail.text: There is no logout endpoint server-side: GET /rest/user/logout returns 500 "Unexpected path" (x18), and no logout route appears in the SPA bundle. Authentication is stateless JWT with no server-side session store or token blacklist, so a token that is captured (e.g. via the non-HttpOnly cookie, cleartext HTTP, or the unauthenticated /rest/memories leak flagged by other lanes) remains usable until its JWT expiry regardless of the user clicking logout. Combined with cleartext transport this materially aids session hijacking.

leads.title: [agent] Session token cookie set without HttpOnly, Secure or SameSite over cleartext HTTP

detail.text: GET /rest/user/whoami with an Authorization: Bearer <jwt> header causes the server to respond with Set-Cookie: token=<jwt>; Path=/ and nothing else — no HttpOnly, no Secure, no SameSite (exchange x7). The host answers only on cleartext http:// (no HTTPS listener, x1/other-lane). Consequences: the session JWT is readable by client-side JavaScript (XSS token theft), transmitted/stored without TLS, and sent automatically on cross-site requests (enabling CSRF against cookie-authenticated endpoints like /profile).

leads.title: [agent] Session/JWT forgery: server accepts unsigned alg:none tokens, enabling impersonation of any user

detail.text: A hand-crafted JWT with header {"typ":"JWT","alg":"none"} and payload {"status":"success","data":{"id":1}} and an empty signature was accepted as a valid session: GET /api/Users returned 200 with the full user table (27 redacted sensitive values incl. deluxeToken and email addresses, x65), GET /rest/basket/1 returned 200 (x66), GET /rest/wallet/balance returned 200 (x67). Control requests prove it is the forged token granting access: no token = 401 (x24), "Bearer garbage.not.ajwt" = 401 (x68), and a well-formed HS256 token with an invalid signature = 401 (x69). The backend therefore skips signature verification for alg:none, so anyone can mint a token for any user id (id=1 is the admin) and fully impersonate them without credentials. Critical session-integrity / authentication-bypass issue. Likely also relevant to the authentication lane.
